title: Emphasis First: Describing the Central Valley

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know fronting with *Crucial fue…* and *En aquella ciudad comenzó…* from B2 Unit 1: you move the piece you want to stress to the front, and the subject goes behind the verb. *De gran importancia son los viñedos* puts the quality first. A place or time phrase can go first too: *Entre las dos cordilleras se extiende el valle*. It works like a climax, so use it once in a paragraph. Here you use it to describe the Central Valley of Chile.

sections.title: What can go first
rows: De gran importancia son los viñedos del valle.
*De* + noun first: the vineyards of the valley are of great importance.
Entre dos cordilleras se extiende el Valle Central.
Place first: between two mountain ranges lies the Central Valley.
En invierno aumenta la contaminación en Santiago.
Time first: in winter the pollution in Santiago increases.
Muy importantes son los ríos que bajan de los Andes.
Adjective first: the rivers that come down from the Andes are very important. (the verb agrees with *los ríos*)

items.spanish: Al este de Santiago se levantan los Andes.
items.english: To the east of Santiago the Andes rise.

items.spanish: De gran importancia son los viñedos del Valle Central.
items.english: The vineyards of the Central Valley are of great importance.

items.spanish: En verano llueve muy poco en el centro de Chile.
items.english: In summer it rains very little in central Chile.

sections.content: The verb agrees with the subject, which now stands after it: *Importantes son los ríos*, not *Importantes es los ríos*. Keep the subject behind the verb: *Importantes los ríos son* sounds unnatural.
